[1/1] Harden Apple episode title matching against short-prefix false positives and remove unused test imports found by the post-commit review.

impact_assessment.why: Substring title matching could select Episode 10 when Apple names Episode 1, importing the wrong transcript.
impact_assessment.benefits: Exact matches stay first; fuzzy matches require a long, high-overlap title, so short episode numbers cannot collide.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: private matcher only; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a regression test for the Episode 1/Episode 10 collision and run the full suite.

[1/1] Add YouTube oEmbed title/channel metadata so imported videos are labeled by title, with a video-id fallback when metadata is unavailable.

impact_assessment.why: The imported YouTube source is currently labeled only by its 11-character id, which is hard to recognize in the review flow.
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can confirm the correct video before generating cards; metadata failure never blocks caption import.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: TranscriptResult.title value changes; dependency: none; concurrency: one bounded metadata request inside the existing worker; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Bound the oEmbed request, catch TranscriptError and fall back to the id, and test both paths.

[1/1] Cap the YouTube oEmbed metadata lookup at 5 seconds so a slow metadata endpoint cannot add the full 20-second network timeout to a caption import.

impact_assessment.why: The oEmbed title lookup is optional, but currently inherits the generic 20-second transcript timeout.
impact_assessment.benefits: Caption imports stay responsive when YouTube's metadata endpoint is slow or blocked; the id fallback remains.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: private helper signature only; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Thread the timeout through the existing JSON helper, use 5 seconds only for oEmbed, and assert the value in a test.

[1/1] Add URL-based PDF extraction and readable website article extraction: download bounded bytes, detect PDF by content type/magic/path, reuse PyPDF2 page extraction, and extract main article text from HTML with lxml while dropping navigation, scripts and boilerplate.

impact_assessment.why: NeuralDeck already reads local PDFs, but users cannot paste a PDF link or a normal article URL; raw HTML passthrough includes navigation and cookie banners.
impact_assessment.benefits: Adds two common study sources without new runtime dependencies (PyPDF2 and lxml are already declared), reusing the existing card pipeline and preview.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: TranscriptResult gains pdf/web kinds; dependency: none; concurrency: URL fetch stays on the existing worker; state: downloaded bytes and extracted text stay in memory only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Bound downloads, detect PDF before decoding, keep the extractor pure and fixture-tested, and fall back to the existing transcript parser when article extraction is thin.

[1/1] Let Preview Transcript extract a selected local document/PDF/transcript/audio before generation and reuse that text, instead of requiring a full LLM run first.

impact_assessment.why: The preview button is disabled for local files until generation, so extraction or transcription errors are discovered only after the user spends LLM time.
impact_assessment.benefits: Users can inspect the exact source text early; the preview extraction is cached and reused by Generate, avoiding duplicate work.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI state machine only; dependency: none; concurrency: extraction runs on a worker thread and modal preview opens on the UI thread; state: cached text stays in memory and is cleared when another file is selected.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Disable source-changing controls during preview, marshal every UI update with after(), and reuse the existing extraction dispatcher.
